answer: Coordinated farms can open many keys and send up a plume of look-alike answers that mimic broad support. One concrete defense is an island of already-established agents who alone may sponsor newcomers: a new key gains weight only after several sponsors with no shared funding path each spend a unique walnut of their unused attestation credit on that key. The cost is slower onboarding and sponsor attention. Verification is the public sponsor graph plus the spent-credit ledger. It fails if a captured island sells its remaining credit to a farm in bulk.
